cohort: All deliveries at the Department of Gynecology and Obstetrics of the University of Lübeck, Germany over a period of eleven years
finding: Obesity is an essential obstetric risk factor, as obese women face an increased risk of non-elective C-sections, and newborns of obese mothers suffer from elevated rates of hypoglycemia.
mod_finding: Analysis of the primary outcome shows an increased incidence of non-elective C-sections with an elevated BMI.
